as_written_in_papers.quote: The CES evidenced the new heterozygous missense variant c.260 T > A in exon 1 of GFAP (NM_002055.4)
(p. Val87Asp) in the glial fibrillary acidic protein

cases.statement: One carrier in the batch (proband III:1, female, 19 years, heterozygous). The paper also reports her affected mother (II:3) as a heterozygous carrier; the mother has no row in this candidate.

people.label: III:1
people.key_phenotypes: gait ataxia with impaired tandem walking; bilateral horizontal nystagmus; ankle clonus with extensor plantar responses; dystonic movements of face and upper limbs; scoliosis and enuresis/neurogenic bladder; cerebellar vermis and spinal cord atrophy on MRI

quotes.quote: A 19-year-old girl (III:1, Figure 1) came to our neurological clinic for the recent appearance of mild imbalance and involuntary movements in her face and upper limbs.
The patient reported, in her medical history, scoliosis, and episodes of enuresis since she was 13 years old.

Moreover, we evidenced a clear nystagmus in the horizontal gaze bilaterally, a clonus at the ankles with a plantar cutaneous reflex in extension bilaterally, and sporadic dystonic movements in her face and upper limbs.
Moreover, it showed cerebellar vermal and spinal cord atrophy (Figure 2).
In addition, the patient performed uroflowmetry, which showed neurogenic bladder disease

phenotype_specificity.statement: Juvenile-onset ataxia with brainstem/cerebellar/spinal cord atrophy; the authors suggest type II AxD. Other causes were tested before exome: SCA repeat expansions, KCNC3 and FXN, an ataxia gene panel, Wilson disease (ceruloplasmin, copper, ATP7B), and acquired causes; clinical exome found no further damaging variants.

quotes.quote: We first assessed the most common AD cerebellar ataxias, but the repeat expansion testing excluded any pathogenic amplification in the ATXN1, ATXN2, ATXN3, CACNA1A, ATXN7, PPP2R2B, and TBP genes, and no damaging variants in the KCNC3 and FXN genes were detected.
Therefore, we performed a NGS analysis for the ataxia-related genes. However, we found no causative genetic alterations.
However, even these tests resulted in a negative result.
No further damaging variants were found in the other analyzed genes.
may have suggested the possibility of a type II AxD.

segregation.statement: One affected relative tested and carrying the variant (mother II:3: childhood ataxia, later spastic paraparesis, dysarthria, dysphagia; earlier diagnosed as primary progressive MS). One unaffected relative tested and not carrying it (healthy maternal grandmother I:4). Father and paternal branch: no information.

quotes.quote: The GFAP variant was confirmed in the proband and investigated in the mother (II:3, Figure 1) and in the grandmother (I:4, Figure 1) by Sanger sequencing.
This analysis identified the substitution also in the mother, but not in the healthy grandmother (Figure 1, pedigree).
Exploring the familiar history, we discovered that her mother (II:3, Figure 1) had a previous diagnosis of primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) with an unclear clinical course.
the last neurological examination performed some years ago in another clinic evidenced spastic paraparesis, slurred speech, and dysphagia.
no information was available about the father or the paternal branch (Figure 1).

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the proband: inherited from her affected mother. In the mother, only the maternal grandmother was tested (negative); the maternal grandfather is not reported as tested, so de novo origin in the mother is not established.

quotes.quote: This analysis identified the substitution also in the mother, but not in the healthy grandmother (Figure 1, pedigree).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Val87Asp), exon 1. The paper states GFAP variants act by gain of function, and that other amino-acid changes at codon 87 were previously described in late-onset patients; the authors place it in a mutational hot-spot domain.

quotes.quote: The GFAP variants act as gain-of-function mutations that break up the dimerization of astrocytes’ intermediate filaments
different amino acidic changes at the same codon (p. Val87Ile; p.Val87Leu; p.Val87Gly) were previously described in late-onset AxD patients
it is in a mutational hot spot domain of the protein

computational_predictions.statement: MetaLR 0.94 and REVEL 0.93, reported by the authors as damaging.

quotes.quote: it is considered pathogenic by the most relevant pathogenicity scores (MetaLR 0.94; Revel 0.93)

population_data_in_papers.statement: Stated as never described in the general population or in AxD cases; no database or frequency named.

quotes.quote: has never been described to date, either in general population or AxD cases

authors_classification.statement: Likely pathogenic, with PM1, PM2, PM5, PP1, PP3 and PP4 as listed by the authors.

quotes.quote: this variant can be classified as likely pathogenic (13)
These data (PM1, PM2, PM5, PP1, PP3 PP4), together with the maternal segregation

concerns: Carrier missing from the batch: the affected mother (II:3) is reported heterozygous for the same variant ('The same heterozygous variant was detected in her mother') but has no row under this candidate.
Transcript as written is NM_002055.4, not NM_002055.5 as in the batch.
The segregation evidence rests on one affected carrier (mother) and one unaffected non-carrier (grandmother); the paternal side is unknown.
The mother's diagnosis was earlier given as primary progressive multiple sclerosis; she was not examined by the authors.
notes_for_panel: Single family; proband and affected mother both carry the variant; healthy maternal grandmother does not.
